stories.title: Automattic debuts a platform to deploy vibe coding apps amid a changing internet
stories.summary: Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com, launched Spacefast, a service for hosting apps made with AI coding tools. It bundles databases, sign-in, file uploads, email and analytics, and competes with Lovable and Emergent.
stories.why: AI-built apps still need somewhere to run; hosting with the basics included lowers the barrier for non-developers shipping real projects.

stories.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Ultrafast now available on AI Gateway
stories.summary: Vercel added a very fast DeepSeek model to its AI Gateway in public preview, served through Fireworks. It can produce over 1,000 tokens per second and has a 1M-token context window.
stories.why: Speed at this level makes interactive tools and agent loops feel instant, and a gateway lets you try it by changing one model name.

stories.title: Your Experts Have Partners. There's HOPE for Keeping Them Together
stories.summary: Amazon researchers describe HOPE, a way to shrink Mixture-of-Experts models by removing experts while accounting for how pairs of experts work together. They report it beat other pruning methods at 50% pruning, including on coding tasks.
stories.why: Smaller versions of big models are cheaper to run, so better pruning could make strong open models practical on modest hardware.

stories.title: Nemotron-Personas-Finance-Japan: A Synthetic Dataset Capturing Japan's Demographics and Financial Context
stories.summary: Elith and NVIDIA released a synthetic dataset of 9 million Japanese personas with financial details, built from official statistics and licensed CC BY 4.0. A companion personal-data model for Japanese launched the same day.
stories.why: Synthetic, openly licensed data lets teams test and tune finance tools for a specific country without touching real customer records.

stories.title: Crusoe sells troubled Wyoming data center project to Google
stories.summary: Data center developer Crusoe confirmed it sold an unfinished Wyoming campus to Google, which reportedly had concerns about cost and timing under Crusoe. Google did not say what it paid but plans to invest $17 billion in the site. Crusoe is still building another data center for Google in Texas.
stories.why: It shows how hard it is for independent builders to deliver giant AI campuses on time, which shapes who ends up controlling compute capacity.

stories.title: Megaspeed exec was recruited to spy on Nvidia CEO, according to US intelligence memo
stories.summary: Media reports describe a memo, reportedly based on US intelligence, claiming an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed was recruited by Chinese intelligence to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Nvidia says it shares no classified information with customers. A separate report questioned a Chinese firm cleared to buy advanced Nvidia chips.
stories.why: The memo's claims are unverified, but stories like this feed pressure for tighter controls on who can buy advanced AI chips.

stories.title: World Models Will Soon Be Inescapable. Here's What You Need to Know
stories.summary: An explainer on world models, AI systems that take in images of a scene and predict what happens next, simulating physics instead of predicting words. Companies like Niantic Spatial, Odyssey and Wayve use them to build realistic practice worlds where robots and driverless cars can train safely.
stories.why: World models are the next big bet after chatbots; knowing how they differ from language models helps make sense of the coming wave of robot and self-driving news.

stories.title: Copilot code review: API management and review overview updates
stories.summary: GitHub now lets teams manage Copilot code review settings through its REST and GraphQL APIs, from enterprise policy down to single repositories. The review summary comment is more compact, and users can say why an overview missed the mark. The update also fixes billing and automatic review bugs.
stories.why: Teams can now script AI code review settings across many repos instead of clicking through each one, making it easier to roll out consistently.

stories.title: Meta introduces Spaces, a new way to collaborate with your Muse agent
stories.summary: Meta launched Spaces for its Muse agents: project-focused areas like trip planners or gift trackers that Muse builds from a chat description. Spaces can connect to other apps and update themselves in the background. Meta says Muse agents reached 10 million users in the US and Canada within two months.
stories.why: Consumer agents are moving from one-off chats to persistent mini-apps they build and maintain, a pattern builders should expect users to want everywhere.

stories.title: OpenAI reportedly raises an additional $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation
stories.summary: Citing a Bloomberg report, TechCrunch says OpenAI has raised $11 billion so far in a round valuing it at $1.25 trillion. The round may reach about $20 billion when it closes, well below the $30 billion target reported in September.
stories.why: A smaller-than-planned raise, alongside talk of a lower Anthropic IPO valuation, suggests investors are getting pickier about AI lab prices.

stories.title: Microsoft moves to consolidate its relationships with neoclouds in AI
stories.summary: Microsoft plans to cut back the number of neocloud providers it rents AI computing from and lean more on its own data centers, according to people familiar with the matter. It has not yet chosen which partners to drop.
stories.why: Neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius depend on a few big customers, so losing Microsoft business could squeeze GPU capacity and prices for everyone else.

stories.title: Free Chinese AI Models Are Getting Scary Good at Hacking
stories.summary: Testing firm Vals had AI models attack simulated company networks. OpenAI's restricted cyber model finished 81 percent of tasks, while the downloadable DeepSeek model managed 73 percent at a fraction of the token cost.
stories.why: If open models nearly match gated ones at hacking, limiting access to frontier models buys less time, and defenders should plan accordingly.

stories.title: @GitHub in Slack and Teams is generally available and more
stories.summary: GitHub's chat assistant for Slack and Microsoft Teams is now generally available. Teams can investigate bugs, file issues, make code changes and open pull requests from inside a conversation, and issues it creates now note which chat they came from.
stories.why: Moving coding work into team chat lets non-developers kick off fixes, so it is worth deciding who on your team should have that power.

stories.title: Egyptian and Nigerian English join the Open ASR Leaderboard
stories.summary: Hugging Face's speech recognition leaderboard added private test sets for Egyptian and Nigerian English, supplied by Liva AI. Keeping the test data private makes it harder for models to be tuned to the benchmark, and results are now grouped by accent family.
stories.why: If your app takes voice input from a global audience, accent-level scores are a better guide for picking a speech model than one overall number.

stories.title: Ramp data shows AI spending stalling just as Anthropic nears its IPO
stories.summary: Ramp's data shows business spending on AI tokens grew just 1.5% across August and September, after 42% in July, then picked up 8.9% in the month to October 23. Its economist blames price cuts and cost controls rather than weak demand.
stories.why: If usage keeps rising while spending flattens, tokens are getting cheaper for builders, but the labs' revenue stories get harder to sustain. The data covers Ramp's own customers, not the whole market.

stories.title: OpenAI released a new cybersecurity model. Is that enough?
stories.summary: OpenAI is offering a new model, ChatGPT Cyber, to the top tier of its Daybreak security program, and says it flagged 948 potential Linux kernel issues. Separately, a startup CTO used GPT 5.6 Sol to find a severe Ubuntu flaw, now patched, with no known exploitation.
stories.why: Serious bugs are getting cheaper to find, for attackers as well as defenders. If you ship code, expect more vulnerability reports and less time to patch them.

stories.title: Palo Alto Networks in talks to buy AI agent security startup Clutch for $500M
stories.summary: Palo Alto Networks is reportedly negotiating to buy Clutch Security for $500 million in cash plus milestone payments, about 50 times its annual recurring revenue. The terms come from an unnamed source, neither company commented, and no deal has been announced.
stories.why: A price that high suggests big security vendors see AI agents and their credentials as a real new risk. Anyone giving agents access to production systems should treat that access as a security question.

stories.title: ToyBlocks: A controlled world for robot learning and evaluation
stories.summary: Ai2 released ToyBlocks, an open simulated world of a robot arm and blocks, with about 85,000 demonstrations. Its layered test setup succeeded in 55.5% of simulated runs and 50% of 30 real-world runs. Ai2 says more trials are needed for statistical confidence.
stories.why: Robot learning is hard to compare because everyone tests differently, so a shared open benchmark helps. The modest scores are a useful check on hype about general-purpose robots.

stories.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash now available on AI Gateway
stories.summary: Vercel added Google's Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash to its AI Gateway. The model makes 3 to 15 second videos with native audio, edits clips using up to six reference images, and can extend videos to 30 seconds, at resolutions up to 4K.
stories.why: Apps already using the gateway can try video generation by changing a model name, without a separate Google integration. Check Google's pricing first, since this page does not list it.

stories.title: Dropbox acquires Tigris Data for $350M to bolster its AI infrastructure
stories.summary: Dropbox agreed to buy Tigris Data, a storage startup built for AI workloads, for about $350 million in cash. It also launched DBX Agent Cloud, starting with standalone S3-compatible object storage. Dropbox expects the deal to close in Q4 2026, per its SEC filing and TechCrunch.
stories.why: A file-sync company buying AI storage shows how much the agent boom is pulling older software firms toward infrastructure. Builders may get another S3-style storage option.

stories.title: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor
stories.summary: Meta bought Conductor, a startup whose app runs several coding agents side by side in separate workspaces. Meta confirmed the deal but shared no price. Conductor's cloud service shuts down November 20, and user cloud data will be deleted after that.
stories.why: Big labs are buying the tools that orchestrate many agents at once. If you use Conductor, export your cloud data before November 20.

stories.title: Google faces backlash for plan that would turn off Search for schools that restrict AI
stories.summary: Google's school software ties Search access to opting in to its AI tools, according to a Google education executive quoted by The New York Times. Senators Bernie Sanders and Richard Blumenthal criticized the plan. Google says Gemini and Search are off by default and schools can switch each on separately.
stories.why: Bundling AI with basic tools is becoming a fight over choice, especially for kids. Expect more pressure for clear AI opt-outs in education products.

stories.title: Axiom Math wants to keep AI slop out of mathematics
stories.summary: Startup Axiom says its AI agents formally checked the Stacks Project, a huge algebraic geometry reference, in the Lean proof language. The company puts it at about 7,654 pages turned into roughly 16 million lines of verified code. Mathematicians quoted say it fills a big gap in formalized math.
stories.why: Machine-checked proofs are one answer to AI output that sounds right but is not. The claim comes from the company, so watch for independent review.

stories.title: A Closer Look at Phonon TTS. Launching High-Quality On-Device Speech That Tops the Benchmarks
stories.summary: Gradium released Phonon, a small text-to-speech model that runs on the device with no server. It comes in two sizes of about 65 and 75 MB, covers five languages, and ships with over 100 voices. The English model is Apache 2.0, and it now works in Hugging Face Transformers.
stories.why: A free, tiny voice model lets you add speech to apps that work offline and cost nothing per call. The benchmark wins are the makers' own claims.

stories.title: AMD's data center revenue nearly doubles in Q3 and CEO Su expects growth to accelerate
stories.summary: AMD reported third-quarter revenue of $13.38 billion, up 45% from a year ago and above estimates. Data center revenue hit a record $8.5 billion and is now about two-thirds of sales. AMD guided to about $17 billion next quarter, and Lisa Su expects server revenue to double in 2027.
stories.why: AMD is the main alternative to Nvidia for AI chips, so its growth affects how much compute is available and what it costs.

stories.title: US voters roundly reject data centers in ballot measures
stories.summary: On Election Day, voters in more than 30 localities across nine states backed moratoriums, bans or other limits on data centers, according to early counts. Edgewater, Florida wrote a ban into its city charter, and Perry, Ohio tightened terms for hyperscaler tax breaks.
stories.why: Local opposition is becoming a real constraint on where AI compute gets built, which could slow new capacity and shift it to friendlier regions.

stories.title: Progress on provable inference for large language models
stories.summary: Anthropic released FlashProve, an open-source prototype that uses zero-knowledge proofs to show an output came from a specific set of model weights without revealing them. It is far costlier than normal inference and limited to short contexts, and no lab plans to deploy it yet.
stories.why: Being able to prove which model produced an answer could help audits and catch providers quietly swapping in cheaper models.

stories.title: StateBench: Testing how language models track state changes over long documents
stories.summary: Ai2 released a benchmark that tests whether models can keep track of things that change across long inputs. Frontier models handle the easier levels but drop to 13% or lower on the hardest, longest problems. In small-model tests, some non-transformer designs generalized far better than transformers.
stories.why: If your app relies on a model following a long, changing document or session, this shows where that can quietly fail.

stories.title: Vercel Security Review now in public beta
stories.summary: Vercel now scans every push to a connected GitHub repo for vulnerabilities, for Pro and Enterprise teams. Each finding comes with a suggested fix and a severity rating, and its agent can open a pull request that still needs approval. Reviews are free until November 10.
stories.why: Automatic security checks on every push are a cheap safety net for small teams shipping AI-written code quickly.

stories.title: Anthropic warns that it's very close to RSI capability, aka self-building AI
stories.summary: Anthropic's revised IPO filing says it may soon reach recursive self-improvement, where AI helps build its own successors. Internal estimates suggest a near-term model could cross a key threshold in its Responsible Scaling Policy, though no current model has been designated as over it.
stories.why: A frontier lab putting this risk in a legal filing raises the stakes for how much human oversight stays in AI development.

stories.title: Brookfield plans for a $27 billion AI data center at UK power station
stories.summary: Drax and Brookfield plan a data center of more than one gigawatt at Drax Power Station in North Yorkshire, with total investment that could pass 20 billion pounds. A first 100 MW phase targets early 2028 but still needs approvals, a tenant and a final investment decision.
stories.why: AI builders are now chasing sites with existing power connections, turning old power stations into some of the most valuable real estate in tech.

stories.title: Apple restricts dating apps and AI companions to users 18 and up
stories.summary: Apple will require apps with dating features or virtual companions that engage in romantic or sexual content to carry an 18+ rating. Developers must declare new content descriptors starting November 16, with a January 2027 deadline for all apps.
stories.why: Anyone shipping a companion or character chatbot on iPhone now faces an adult-only rating, which limits reach and changes the business case.

stories.title: GitHub Copilot is now available in JetBrains Air
stories.summary: Copilot can now be chosen as a coding agent inside JetBrains Air through the Agent Client Protocol. Tasks run locally in a JetBrains IDE or in isolated cloud containers through Air Teams, and cloud usage is billed to your Copilot plan.
stories.why: Coding agents are becoming plug-ins that work across editors, so teams can keep their tools and swap the agent behind them.

stories.title: Wave Forcing: Towards Speed-of-Light Streaming Video Generation
stories.summary: Researchers describe a way to generate video as a continuous stream fast enough to play live, reaching about 135 frames per second on eight H200 GPUs. Videos show much more motion than earlier methods, though the authors note more camera drift.
stories.why: Live AI video opens the door to interactive uses like games and real-time avatars, but it still needs costly hardware.

stories.title: Anthropic reports $17 billion in Q3 revenue, purchase commitments of $895.4 billion in revised S-1
stories.summary: Anthropic filed an amended IPO prospectus with third-quarter numbers: about $17 billion in revenue, with quarter-over-quarter growth slowing to roughly 47 percent. The nine-month net loss of $104 billion comes mostly from non-cash revaluation of convertible notes. Purchase and lease commitments total about $895 billion, nearly all for compute.
stories.why: This is the most detailed public look at a frontier lab's economics so far, and the compute obligations show how capital-heavy the model business has become.

stories.title: Marvell to buy Lumentum in all-stock deal, a massive bet on AI connectivity
stories.summary: Marvell will acquire optical components maker Lumentum in an all-stock deal that values Lumentum at an implied $115 billion enterprise value. The companies say optical links between AI chips are central to data center design. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2028.
stories.why: One of the largest chip deals on record, and a sign that the next AI infrastructure bottleneck is the networking between accelerators, not just the accelerators themselves.

stories.title: Evaluate Vercel Flags from another project without sharing SDK keys
stories.summary: Vercel added Project Connections, which let one project read feature flags defined in another project on the same team without copying a server SDK key into its environment. Connected deployments authenticate with their own identity, access is read-only, and a connection can be revoked without redeploying.
stories.why: If you run several small Vercel sites, you can now manage one set of flags for all of them with no shared secrets to rotate.

stories.title: Apriel Voice 27B Preview: An Open Model for Speech, Reasoning, and Tool Use
stories.summary: A new open speech model built on Gemma 4 takes spoken input directly and produces both answers and tool calls from a single backbone, with no separate speech-to-text step. Training happens in two stages: first the speech interface, then the whole model, while keeping its text and image abilities.
stories.why: An open-weight voice model that can reason and call tools lowers the bar for building voice agents without chaining three separate models together.

stories.title: A Defense Contractor Gave Their Personal AI Agent Access to a Secure Pentagon System
stories.summary: WIRED reports, citing anonymous sources, that an Accenture employee connected a personal Claude account to a Pentagon network holding controlled unclassified information so an AI agent could write and deploy code. The agent ran for about two months before it was found. Accenture says an independent investigation found the allegations without merit.
stories.why: Personal coding agents can slip past procurement bans and contractor security rules, which is the gap federal incident-reporting and supply-chain policy is now trying to close.

stories.title: Judge allows NAACP lawsuit over xAI data center pollution to move forward
stories.summary: A federal judge refused to dismiss a Clean Air Act suit accusing xAI of running at least 35 gas turbines at its Memphis-area Colossus site without air permits. She rejected xAI's claim that the turbines are mobile and exempt.
stories.why: Permitting and pollution rules are becoming a real constraint on where AI compute can be built and how fast, not just a local nuisance.

stories.title: OpenAI reportedly lowers funding target for new round
stories.summary: TechCrunch relays reports that OpenAI cut its target to $20 billion from an earlier $30 billion. The Wall Street Journal says $11 billion is secured so far and some large investors were lukewarm. OpenAI had not yet commented.
stories.why: Investor caution on AI spending could affect how aggressively labs price and expand. The figures are second-hand, via the FT and WSJ.

stories.title: Anthropic expected to receive high 'junk' rating from credit agencies following IPO, FT report says
stories.summary: Per the Financial Times, Blackstone told investors it expects a double-B rating for Anthropic after its IPO, lower than an earlier investment-grade forecast. That would make borrowing for compute costlier. Anthropic and Blackstone declined to comment.
stories.why: A lab's financing costs shape its compute plans and possibly pricing. This is one report's expectation, not an actual rating.

stories.title: Route and orchestrate models with GitHub Copilot Fusion
stories.summary: GitHub made Copilot Fusion generally available. You pick it in the model picker with an effort level, and it chooses models per prompt, using one model, a fallback cascade, or one model critiquing another.
stories.why: Automatic routing means less manual model picking in Copilot. Benchmark and cost claims are GitHub's own, so test it on your work.

stories.title: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts
stories.summary: Parameter Labs describes chaining a message handler, an unsandboxed iframe injection and a permissive content security policy to run script on ChatGPT. Per the post, OpenAI fixed it and paid a bounty.
stories.why: A clear example of AI chat apps inheriting classic web security risks when they render user-made HTML. Worth knowing if you let models generate previewable apps.

stories.title: Building a Haunted House with NVIDIA Nemotron Open Models
stories.summary: An NVIDIA engineer built MonsterHouse, a talking Halloween character projected onto a garage that chats with trick-or-treaters. It runs on one two-GPU workstation using open Nemotron models for speech recognition, conversation and costume spotting, with about 1.7 seconds of median response time.
stories.why: It is a concrete recipe for a fully local voice agent built from open models, showing that real-time voice characters no longer need a cloud API.

stories.title: Vercel Daemons can now call services with bindings
stories.summary: Vercel Daemons can now call other private services in the same deployment by declaring a binding in config. Vercel handles the routing, authentication and TLS, and passes the target's address in an environment variable. Bindings work in one direction only.
stories.why: Long-running agent workers on Vercel can now talk to private backend services without exposing them publicly or hand-rolling auth.

stories.title: Nvidia weighs playing the cosigner for Nscale's AI data center in West Virginia
stories.summary: Nvidia is reportedly in talks to guarantee billions in debt for Nscale's West Virginia data center, which is contracted to serve Anthropic. If Nscale missed construction payments, Nvidia would temporarily take over the site. The report credits The Information.
stories.why: Chipmakers backing their customers' debt shows how much of the AI buildout rests on a few balance sheets, which affects how stable compute supply and prices will be.

stories.title: Was this the AI election?
stories.summary: Ahead of the 2026 midterms, Transformer looks at whether AI is a real campaign issue. Polls show very few voters rank it first, but many battleground campaigns mention AI or data centers. The authors argue it feeds worries about jobs, corruption and power bills.
stories.why: Data centers and electricity costs are turning AI into a local political issue, which can shape where new compute gets built and how it is regulated.

stories.title: LLM use is acknowledged almost as often as specialized AI tools in biology preprints
stories.summary: Epoch AI found that about 17% of bioRxiv biology preprints now acknowledge using large language models, close to the 19% that cite specialized AI tools such as AlphaFold. Use of LLMs for the analysis itself, not just writing, rose to about 4% by September.
stories.why: General chat models are quietly becoming part of the scientific workflow, not just a writing aid, which raises the stakes for their accuracy in research settings.

stories.title: Governor Hochul Signs Nation-Leading Legislation to Protect Kids from AI Chatbots
stories.summary: New York's governor signed a law requiring chatbot companies to block certain features for users under 18 and for anyone not confirmed as an adult, such as bots posing as human, claiming romantic ties, or promoting self-harm. Age checks must offer more than one method, and the attorney general can seek civil penalties of up to $25,000 per violation.
stories.why: If you ship a consumer chatbot, age assurance and behavior limits are now a legal requirement in a large state, not a design choice. Expect other states to copy this template.

stories.title: Microsoft recorded $10 billion in revenue from OpenAI last quarter
stories.summary: TechCrunch reports that Microsoft's quarterly filing shows $10 billion in revenue from its commercial arrangements with OpenAI, close to 11 percent of Microsoft's total for the quarter. Amounts OpenAI owed Microsoft rose to $7.2 billion, and Microsoft's stake in OpenAI slipped to 24 percent. The filing does not separate revenue sharing from Azure usage.
stories.why: The two companies compete for enterprise customers yet remain deeply tied financially. That dependence shapes pricing, model access, and how long the partnership holds.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and Granary v2: open speech model and dataset
stories.summary: NVIDIA released an open-weight speech model that transcribes 40 languages, translates to and from English in 31, labels up to 8 speakers, and answers questions about audio up to an hour long. It serves with vLLM or SGLang-Omni on a single GPU. The companion Granary v2 dataset adds about 463,000 hours of speech across 48 languages.
stories.why: A single open checkpoint covering transcription, translation, and speaker labeling lowers the cost of building voice features without a paid API. Note it handles recorded audio only, not live streams.

stories.title: Octoverse: Commits, pushes reach new highs in 2026 as developers build with agents
stories.summary: GitHub's annual Octoverse report counts 17.9 billion pushes and 1.3 billion merged pull requests in the year to September 30. Agents opened more than 40 percent of pull requests in September, up from 17 percent in March. Paying Copilot users spread their requests across 47 different models, with no single model above 25 percent.
stories.why: Agent-written code is now a large share of real work on the biggest code host, so review practices and CI need to assume it. The model mix shows developers are not locking into one vendor.

stories.title: As AI agents reshape the web, Google opens Gemini and Search to more apps
stories.summary: TechCrunch reports Google announced a Connected Apps Platform that lets businesses plug their apps into Gemini and Search so users can take actions inside them. Developers integrate through a cloud-hosted MCP server or Android app functions and manage the connection in a new Google Connected Console. It is a US public preview behind a waitlist.
stories.why: Being reachable inside Gemini and Search may matter for app discovery the way search ranking once did. The MCP route means an existing server can be a starting point.

stories.title: Early progress on accelerating drug development with Claude
stories.summary: Anthropic says it has worked for several months with six drug developers and started its own programs, including one for a rare childhood muscular dystrophy. In one example Claude produced about 35,000 antibody designs for a food-allergy drug in roughly a month, and early lab tests found a few that work. These are early results from Anthropic's own account.
stories.why: First hard numbers on AI designing real drug candidates, from the company itself. Read it as a claim to be tested, not a result.

stories.title: Bank of America asks customers not to share banking passwords with AI assistants
stories.summary: Bank of America emailed customers telling them never to give their username and password to an AI tool or agent, and warned that customers are responsible for what happens with that access. A bank spokesperson confirmed the email is real. Banks are still working out how agents could safely reach accounts.
stories.why: The first big bank drawing a line on AI agents touching accounts. Expect others to follow, and expect agent products to need a bank-approved way in.

stories.title: GitHub Copilot supports server-to-server authentication
stories.summary: In public preview, services and agents built with the Copilot SDK can act for an organization through a GitHub App instead of a signed-in user's credentials. That helps with agents that run unattended. Usage is billed to the organization and its model policies apply.
stories.why: Unattended agents need their own identity, not a borrowed login. GitHub building that plumbing is a sign agents are becoming normal infrastructure.

stories.title: Google's Genie 4 world model adds audio, more realistic worlds, and real-time steering
stories.summary: DeepMind released Genie 4 in research preview. It generates interactive worlds with real-time audio, lets users change the scene mid-simulation with new prompts, and holds scenes for up to two minutes, double Genie 3. Only TechCrunch's report was found, not Google's own post.
stories.why: Interactive video worlds are moving from demo to tool. Audio and live steering are what games and robot training both need.

stories.title: The October inflection point for vibe game development
stories.summary: Developer Simon Willison writes that Claude Opus 5.5 can now produce genuinely fun games. He shows four browser games, including one built from a single prompt with three.js. It is one developer's first-hand account.
stories.why: A careful developer saying a model crossed a quality line is a better signal than a benchmark. Worth trying one prompt yourself.
